Behind the boards

A small arcade,
built for class.

Familiar games, simple rules, and a little time to think.

Pocket Arcade brings seven games together in one place. Click a tile, turn a card or connect a dot: the board and score update as you play.

Seven ways to take a break

Minesweeper is a small deduction puzzle. Memory Match tests how much you remember. Connect the Dots reveals simple drawings, and Tic-tac-toe is for two people sharing one screen.

What happens to my scores?

Games and saved results share one arcade page. Switching its game tabs preserves progress. Save session records a snapshot of your current round; saving it again updates that snapshot. Refreshing or closing the arcade tab clears everything. There is no browser storage.

Built for the Web Programming course

The site uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no libraries or frameworks. The game logic uses variables, conditions and loops. Small functions, click handlers and page updates let the games respond directly on the page; these additions are explained separately in the project report.

No account needed

Everything runs in the browser, including the game rules. There is no database, sign-in, external font or game service.
